issue: On federal habeas review of a state conviction, must a state court's harmless-error determination receive AEDPA deference under 28 U.S.C. § 2254(d)(1), or may a federal court skip AEDPA and grant relief under Brecht alone?

sides.position: Brecht alone governs; AEDPA deference does not apply to a state court's harmless-error determination, and a federal court may grant relief on a showing of actual prejudice under Brecht without first finding the state ruling unreasonable.

Courts must apply both Brecht and AEDPA when reviewing a state court's harmless-error determination; the petitioner must show the state court's ruling was an unreasonable application of clearly established federal law.
cases: Mansfield v. Sec'y, Dep't of Corr., 679 F.3d 1301 (11th Cir. 2012)

this_court: Brecht alone governs; AEDPA deference does not apply to state harmless-error determinations (the panel majority, Davenport, adhered to this view on rehearing en banc denial).
quote: It appears that we are alone in taking a “straight to Brecht approach” in determining on habeas review whether a state court’s constitutional error was harmless.
cite: Ervine Davenport v. Duncan MacLaren, No. 17-2267 (6th Cir. 2020)
